title: Establish Your Vision
hook: The branch floor plan gets useful only when the future tells Alice what to cut this week.
counterintuition: A vision can sound inspiring and still be useless if it never governs sacrifice; the useful turn is to make today's tradeoffs point toward a future worth protecting.
tryThisNow: Write one sentence that describes the life or team result your current 12 week effort is meant to serve.
keyTakeaway: Draft a vision vivid enough to organize sacrifice and close enough to guide the next 12 week cycle. The standard is visible action, not a better-sounding intention.

The vision earns its place when it helps the team cut a pleasant option for a future that matters more.

examples.title: Alice redraws the branch future

planSpec.audience: a practitioner in public library branch vision session who needs the chapter move under real pressure
planSpec.stakes: the visible result will slip while everyone can still explain the effort
planSpec.requiredBeat: Alice turns a vague branch dream into a concrete future residents can feel.

examples.scenario: Sticky notes ring the public library floor plan like small warning flags. Alice must decide whether “serve the community better” stays on the poster or becomes a future residents can picture: fewer parents leaving before story hour, newcomers finding job forms without asking twice, teens staying after school because one corner finally feels theirs.
examples.whatToDo: Translate the branch dream into three resident outcomes people could notice in the building, then choose the one 12 week sacrifice that serves them first.
examples.whyItMatters: A vivid future gives Alice a reason to cut lesser work. The vision becomes useful when residents can feel what the next cycle is buying.

examples.title: Vincent makes the offsite choose

planSpec.audience: a decision-maker in startup leadership offsite choosing whether to protect execution or drift
planSpec.stakes: the next 12 weeks will inherit a soft plan unless the decision is made now
planSpec.requiredBeat: Vincent asks each leader to write the future the offsite must serve.

examples.scenario: At 9:00 a.m. in the offsite room, Vincent looks at name cards around the conference table. As startup lead, he must decide whether every project gets defended or the customer future makes four projects wait.
examples.whatToDo: Have each leader write the future the offsite must serve in one concrete paragraph before anyone argues for a project.
examples.whyItMatters: The offsite needs a filter, not more enthusiasm. Vincent uses vision to expose which sacrifices have a reason behind them.

examples.title: Marit gives retention a face

planSpec.audience: a team lead in nursing unit retention plan who needs visible proof before the week softens
planSpec.stakes: the team will mistake motion for progress if the proof stays hidden
planSpec.requiredBeat: Marit connects retention pain to a future unit nurses want.

examples.scenario: You are looking at exit interviews clipped by shift, and every page sounds tired in a different way. Marit must decide whether to chase another staffing metric or name the unit nurses want to stay in: predictable handoffs, no double-charting after midnight, and a charge nurse who can actually coach.
examples.whatToDo: Turn the retention pain into a picture of the unit people would choose to remain in, then tie the first 12 week push to one part of that picture.
examples.whyItMatters: Retention becomes stronger when it points toward a lived future. Marit gives the team more than a complaint to escape.

examples.title: Matteo sees the loading bay differently

planSpec.audience: a reflective operator in urban food rescue expansion reading last week's failure as evidence
planSpec.stakes: a repeat failure will be explained away instead of corrected
planSpec.requiredBeat: Matteo pictures the food rescue result before choosing expansion work.

examples.scenario: It took Matteo two cold mornings beside the loading bay to realize the expansion plan had no future in it. Coolers waited, volunteers apologized, and the map kept growing. On Friday he rewrites the goal around one image: three shelters receiving fresh meals before noon without a single frantic phone call.
examples.whatToDo: Picture the service result before choosing expansion work. Matteo should let that result decide which routes, partners, and pickups deserve the next cycle.
examples.whyItMatters: Expansion can become ego in operational clothing. A clear future keeps the food rescue focused on the people served, not the size of the map.

examples.title: Nina puts students inside the vision

planSpec.audience: a reader in secondary school arts department comparing intention before the move with proof after it
planSpec.stakes: the work will stay aspirational unless the action changes in the room
planSpec.requiredBeat: Nina turns the arts department vision into student-facing proof.

examples.scenario: Paint-splattered stools crowd the storage room before Nina changes the department plan. Before, the arts vision promised creativity for every student. After, she names the visible proof: ninth graders choosing materials without permission, a critique wall that changes weekly, and a spring show with first-year work at eye level.
examples.whatToDo: Define the student-facing proof the arts department would show if the vision were real, then schedule the first visible change.
examples.whyItMatters: Nina makes the vision testable. Students should be able to experience the future, not merely hear adults endorse it.

examples.title: Aman names the sacrifice

planSpec.audience: two colleagues in Stockholm hardware lab forcing the commitment into plain speech
planSpec.stakes: a public promise will dissolve unless someone names the proof and owner
planSpec.requiredBeat: Aman writes the lab future that makes the next sacrifice worth it.

examples.scenario: Which future makes us willing to kill the side prototype? Aman asks in the Stockholm hardware lab. Sensor boards rest in anti-static bags while the team must decide between keeping every experiment alive or writing the lab future that makes one painful sacrifice clean.
examples.whatToDo: Name the lab future in terms of the customer, the device, and the proof date, then let that future eliminate one attractive distraction.
examples.whyItMatters: Aman turns vision into courage. The sacrifice feels less arbitrary when people can see what it protects.
